message.content: {"0": {"original": "The proposed Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA) was defeated in a pleny", "rephrased": "The European Parliament decisively rejected the proposed Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA), a secretive deal that activists argued threatened internet freedom and access to medicines, with 478 votes cast against it compared to only 39 in favor.", "summary": "The European Parliament rejected the secretive ACTA deal by a large margin."}, "1": {"original": "attributed their success to mobilising the public to bring pressure to bear on", "rephrased": "Activist groups across Europe attribute the successful defeat of the Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA) in the European Parliament to their strategy of mobilizing the general public to apply direct pressure on elected representatives.", "summary": "Activists credit public mobilization for defeating the ACTA legislation."}, "2": {"original": "cautioned that Karel de Gucht deferred any decision on how the Commission will", "rephrased": "The UK's Open Rights Group cautions that the European Commission, under the leadership of Trade Commissioner Karel de Gucht, has deferred any decision on the future of the Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA) pending a ruling from the European Court of Justice regarding its compatibility with European law.", "summary": "The Open Rights Group notes the Commission is delaying ACTA decisions until a court ruling."}, "3": {"original": "The secretive Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA) provoked massive rallie", "rephrased": "The secretive Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA) provoked massive public opposition across Europe, evidenced by widespread demonstrations and a petition gathering two million signatures, which ultimately contributed to its defeat in the European Parliament.", "summary": "Massive public opposition and a two-million-signature petition led to ACTA's defeat."}}
